# Meridian Capital Partners — Annual Risk Report 2025

## Executive Summary

Meridian Capital Partners delivered a total return of 12.4% in 2025, outperforming the benchmark Russell 2000 by 310 basis points. The portfolio benefited from an overweight to healthcare technology and an underweight to regional banks during the first half, when regional bank stress re-emerged following the closure of two mid-sized institutions in the Midwest. Currency tailwinds contributed approximately 40 basis points as the dollar weakened against a basket of emerging market currencies.

Looking ahead to 2026, the investment committee identifies three primary themes: (1) continued AI infrastructure buildout favoring semiconductor capital equipment suppliers; (2) a cyclical recovery in industrials driven by onshoring of supply chains; and (3) selective opportunities in distressed commercial real estate as refinancing walls become due for overleveraged sponsors.

## Portfolio Positioning

As of December 31, 2025, the fund held 78 long positions and 32 short positions across 11 GICS sectors. The top five long positions represented 31.2% of gross exposure, consistent with the fund's moderate concentration policy. Net exposure stood at 58%, down from 64% at the end of 2024, reflecting the committee's cautious stance entering a year with elevated macroeconomic uncertainty.

Technology remained the largest sector allocation at 24.3% of gross long exposure, followed by Healthcare at 18.7% and Industrials at 14.2%. The Energy allocation was trimmed from 9.1% to 5.4% following profit-taking after strong performance in the first quarter. Consumer Discretionary was added to the short book as the committee anticipated margin compression from higher labor costs and slowing unit volume growth.

Fixed income overlays were maintained through interest rate swap positions with a net DV01 of negative $42,000, providing partial insulation against a potential reversal of the 2025 rate-cutting cycle.

## Risk Metrics

Value at Risk (VaR) at the 95th percentile for a one-day holding period was $4.1 million as of year-end, representing 0.82% of net asset value. This compares to $5.6 million at year-end 2024, a 27% reduction attributable to de-risking in the second half and improved diversification following the addition of 12 new positions in previously underrepresented sectors.

Maximum drawdown during 2025 was 6.8%, occurring between March 14 and April 22 when geopolitical tensions in the Middle East drove a risk-off move across equity markets. The portfolio recovered fully within 34 trading days, consistent with the fund's historical pattern of swift recovery following market dislocations.

Sector concentration risk remains the most significant risk factor identified in the annual review. The committee will implement a revised sector limit framework in Q1 2026, capping any single GICS sector at 30% of gross long exposure and 20% of gross short exposure.

## Compliance and Operational Notes

All trades during 2025 complied with the fund's investment policy statement. No material operational incidents were recorded. The fund completed its annual SOC 2 Type II audit in November 2025 with no exceptions noted. The prime broker relationship with Goldman Sachs was renewed under improved terms, reflecting the fund's growth in assets under management.

The fund manager, Sarah Whitmore, and the risk officer, David Chen, have each confirmed their continued compliance with the fund's Code of Ethics and personal trading policies.
